title: DNS over HTTPS causes long buffering in YouTube
body: I am using Firefox 127 on Windows 10. If I set DNS over HTTPS to Max Protection with Cloudflare and hard-refresh a YouTube video, there is consistently a delay of at least 10 seconds, sometimes 30 seconds or more. The video can also freeze around the 20-second mark. The Network Monitor shows many NS_BINDING_ABORTED entries for videoplayback requests, which are absent when DNS over HTTPS is disabled. With DNS over HTTPS completely disabled, videos load nearly instantly and do not pause. Max Protection makes the problem completely consistent; Default or Increased Protection only trigger it sometimes. I attached a screenshot of the Network Monitor.

symptoms_visible: With DNS over HTTPS set to Max Protection using Cloudflare, a hard-refreshed YouTube video takes at least 10 seconds and sometimes more than 30 seconds to start.
The video sometimes freezes around the 20-second mark, and the Network Monitor shows many NS_BINDING_ABORTED videoplayback requests.
With DNS over HTTPS disabled, the same videos load nearly instantly and do not pause.
N0.label: N0 YouTube delay with DoH reported

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the long YouTube delay in a new profile where the only setting I changed is DNS over HTTPS to Max Protection with Cloudflare.
I can also reproduce it on my laptop, but not in a Windows sandbox instance.
The delay remains on another clean profile after changing hardware acceleration and decoder settings.
N1.label: N1 clean profiles and network log collected

symptoms_visible: My ISPs do not support IPv6, and the YouTube delay still occurs with Max Protection.
The same behavior occurs on two other IPv4-only ISP connections, while it does not occur when using a mobile connection that supports IPv6.
Cloudflare is not the only affected provider; buffering has also been seen with NextDNS and Quad9.
N2.label: N2 IPv6 availability correlation established

symptoms_visible: The provided test build played correctly through a couple dozen hard refreshes without a single failure.
In Firefox 127.0.1 with a new profile, enabling network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family made Max Protection fail less often, but only about half of the attempts succeeded.
The installed Firefox 127.0.1 build can still show the long delay.
N3.label: N3 candidate build verified and pref probe measured

symptoms_visible: With DNS over HTTPS enabled, YouTube videos start normally and continue playing without the long initial delay or the pause around 20 seconds.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this in a new profile created through about:profiles?
In a clean profile, which setting do you have to change before the delay appears?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried a new profile and could reproduce it consistently. The only setting I changed was DNS over HTTPS to Max Protection with Cloudflare.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It does not happen in a new profile; it only happens in my normal profile with my extensions enabled.
It also reproduces in a new profile, but I selected NextDNS instead of Cloudflare.

question_patterns: Does the same problem occur on another physical machine?
Can you compare another computer or Windows environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried it on my laptop as well and reproduced it there. I could not reproduce it in a Windows sandbox instance.

question_patterns: What happened in the Windows sandbox or virtual environment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I couldn't reproduce the delay in the Windows sandbox. Installing and enabling uBlock Origin and Privacy Badger there did not make it appear.

question_patterns: Does enabling the same kinds of extensions in the sandbox trigger the delay?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. I enabled uBlock Origin and Privacy Badger in the sandbox and still couldn't reproduce it.

question_patterns: Does about:support list any important modified preferences that might affect networking?
Have you manually changed any relevant about:config preferences?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the modified preferences and didn't see anything important. In the new profile, the only setting I changed was DNS over HTTPS.

question_patterns: Can you capture a networking log from about:logging while reproducing the delay and send it to the Necko team?
Please reproduce this in the clean profile, download the HTTP log, and share it.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the log. The first email address rejected both the attachment and my Drive link, but after you gave me <email-scrubbed> I sent the log there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log is around 12 MB instead of 8 MB, and I shared it using Dropbox.

edges.comment: Comments 1-5 are folded into one user side. Clean-profile reproduction and a second physical machine rule against a profile-specific extension or preference explanation. Another affected user also reported that fresh profiles and hardware/decoder changes retained the observable delay.

question_patterns: Does the affected ISP connection provide working IPv6?
Can you check whether IPv6 is available on the networks where this reproduces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My ISPs do not support IPv6 either.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: IPv6 works normally on every affected connection, and the same delay occurs when I directly connect to IPv6-only sites.
My router advertises IPv6, but my ISP does not provide usable IPv6 connectivity.

edges.comment: Comments 6-8 are merged into the simulated user side. A second affected user reproduced on two ISPs without IPv6 and reported that switching to an IPv6-capable mobile carrier removed the delay. Other users also saw buffering with NextDNS and Quad9, so Cloudflare alone is not the deciding factor.

question_patterns: Could you try this test build and report whether the delay still occurs?
Please hard-refresh several YouTube videos in the provided build and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the build and it worked flawlessly. I hard-refreshed a couple dozen times and it didn't fail a single time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test build still takes 10 to 30 seconds to start on nearly every hard refresh.
The test build worked on twenty hard refreshes instead of a couple dozen.

question_patterns: In a new Firefox 127.0.1 profile, can you enable network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family and report whether Max Protection still stalls?
Please toggle network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family in a test profile and compare repeated hard refreshes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled it in a new profile using Firefox 127.0.1. Max Protection seemed to fail less frequently, but it was still only around a 50% success rate.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After enabling the preference, every hard refresh starts immediately and I cannot reproduce the delay at all.

question_patterns: Can you capture another networking log with the retry preference enabled while the issue still occurs?
Please share an HTTP log from one of the remaining failed attempts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here's a link with two logs: https://we.tl/t-SXzZXUWxpS. The link expires in seven days.

edges.comment: Comments 9-15. Both the provided build test and the about:config toggle are handler-initiated measurements. The user reports only observed outcomes and the raw log link; identifying the HTTP/3 and fallback mechanism is engineer-side analysis.

solution.intent: Correct Firefox's HTTP/3 fallback handling so that an unusable IPv6 attempt on an IPv4-only network can successfully fall back to the working connection, then have the user verify normal YouTube playback in a build containing the correction.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a Firefox build containing the SpeculativeTransaction fallback correction. The networking logs showed that Firefox first attempted an HTTP/3 connection to YouTube over an IPv6 address on a connection without IPv6, then created a fallback connection but failed to accept it because the speculative transaction closed with NS_OK rather than NS_BASE_STREAM_CLOSED. The patch treats that close path as a successful fallback. Please retest repeated YouTube hard refreshes in the updated build before considering the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied network logs, IPv6 availability observations, and build-test results. Engineers derived the mechanism from those logs: the initial HTTP/3 connection selected an IPv6 YouTube address that could not connect, a fallback was started, and SpeculativeTransaction rejected that otherwise usable fallback because it treated only NS_BASE_STREAM_CLOSED—not NS_OK—as success.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from comments 13-21: adjust SpeculativeTransaction's success check so the fallback connection is usable. Uplift, train, ESR relanding, and bot activity are intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause from the networking evidence: Firefox attempted HTTP/3 to a YouTube IPv6 address on a network without usable IPv6, then failed to use the fallback connection because SpeculativeTransaction did not accept the NS_OK close reason as success.

Must ground the diagnosis in the clean-profile reproduction, lack of IPv6 on affected networks, networking logs, and the successful provided test build rather than blaming extensions, hardware acceleration, decoders, or Cloudflare alone.

Must recommend the fallback-handling correction or an update containing it; network.http.http3.retry_different_ip_family must not be presented as the complete fix because it still left roughly half of attempts failing.
Must not treat disabling DNS over HTTPS permanently as the technical resolution.
Must have the reporter verify repeated YouTube hard refreshes on a build containing the correction before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Firefox user who can create clean profiles, inspect Network Monitor and modified preferences, capture about:logging output, change a named about:config preference, and install a provided test build.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise; follows diagnostic instructions carefully, reports exact repetition rates and cross-machine differences, and asks whether additional logs are needed.
